quarterly_data.signal: AEP's 10-K: in October 2025 AEP announced a $72 billion capital plan for 2026-2030 driven by transmission and distribution infrastructure upgrades and new generation to support anticipated load growth. Management forecasts approximately $12.2 billion of capital expenditures in 2026 and $59.7 billion for the four-year period 2027 through 2030, reflecting planned investments in transmission infrastructure and new generation resources to support existing customers and forecasted large load increases.
quarterly_data.figure: $72 billion 2026-2030 capital plan (announced October 2025); 2026 capex ~$12.2 billion; 2027-2030 capex $59.7 billion

players.product: solid-oxide fuel cells for data-center onsite power

connects_to.relationship: on-site fuel cells supplied as bridging power for AEP large-load customers

contracts.signal: AEP's 10-K: in the fourth quarter of 2024 AEP Development Services (Devco), a wholly-owned AEP subsidiary, executed a purchase agreement with Bloom Energy to acquire 100 MWs of solid oxide fuel cells. Under an affiliated services agreement Devco is to design, procure, construct and ultimately sell customer-sited, behind-the-meter fuel cell generation facilities to AEP's Ohio Power (OPCo), which will own and operate them and sell the power they produce to its commercial customers under customer-sited renewable energy resource agreements. Devco's construction work in progress was $480 million as of December 31, 2025 versus $457 million a year earlier.
contracts.units: 100 MWs of solid oxide fuel cells
